items.summary: Text-to-speech (TTS) based on masked diffusion models (MDMs) achieves competitive zero-shot speech synthesis performance. Unlike autoregressive (AR) models, MDMs define a corruption process that maps clean speech-token sequences to masked maps and learn a reverse denoising process to recover the reference tokens.

items.title: What Does LALM Post-training Learn? Rethinking Audio Understanding and Reasoning Capabilities
items.summary: Post-training often improves the performance of large audio-language models on audio understanding and reasoning benchmarks. However, these improvements may reflect adaptation to specific question formats, such as multiple-choice questions, rather than genuine advances in audio understanding and reasoning capabilities.

items.title: Point-and-Play: Instrument Timbre Cloning from Music Mixtures
items.summary: Neural instrument synthesizers can clone the timbre of a solo instrument, letting music producers make music with the sound they desire. In this work, we propose Point-and-Play, a system that clones the timbre of a cued source directly from a polyphonic mixture and uses it to synthesize new pitches and velocities.

items.title: Continued fractions and passive ladder networks for acoustic impedances: the baffled piston and the horn
items.summary: Lumped-element networks give transparent, passive models of acoustic impedances whose low- and high-frequency limits can be read from the circuit, but a systematic, arbitrarily accurate construction for non-rational impedances is lacking.

items.title: CochlearMark: Audio Watermarking via Phase Locked Auditory Nerve Representations
items.summary: Modern audio watermarks achieve strong robustness with learned encoder-decoder models, but their behavior under new processing is established empirically. CochlearMark is introduced as a training-free audio watermark that uses auditory-nerve phase-locking as its feature representation.

items.title: Full-Order Safety for Nonlinear Reduced-Order MPC
items.summary: Reduced-order models (ROMs) make model predictive control (MPC) of high-dimensional nonlinear systems tractable, but the resulting modeling error can lead to constraint violations on the real system. We introduce CoRE-MPC, a robust MPC formulation that plans with a nonlinear ROM and guarantees recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction for the full-order system.

items.title: PACER: Process-Aware VLA Policy Learning from Human Corrections for Robotic Disassembly
items.summary: Robotic disassembly of end-of-life (EoL) products requires robots to accommodate product variation, follow prerequisite sequences, and approach components precisely for contact-rich manipulation. The policy's own rollouts record its approach attempts, and human corrections demonstrate recovery from its errors, but turning these experiences into better policy performance remains challenging.

items.title: End-to-End Vision-Language-Action Policies for Autonomous Lunar Rover Docking
items.summary: Surface navigation on the Moon is subject to extreme illumination contrast and deployment-time perceptual disturbances. While modular navigation pipelines have long supported planetary rover navigation, robustness is compromised by measurement errors that propagate through hand-engineered components.

items.title: A Mode-Unified, Continuous, and Biomimetic Control Strategy of a Robotic Lower Limb Prosthesis
items.summary: Existing biomimetic lower-limb prosthesis controllers are commonly designed for discrete locomotion modes, requiring separate parameterizations for level walking, ramps, and stairs. We present a mode-unified prosthesis control framework that represents knee and ankle biomechanics continuously as functions of terrain slope and gait phase across those locomotion conditions.

items.title: FACT: A Multimodal Force-Action-Track Foundation Model for Human-to-Robot Dexterity
items.summary: Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative to costly robot data collection for dexterous manipulation, but most human datasets lack force measurements. We present FACT, a robot foundation model that cascades from prospective visual planning to force-aware refinement for dexterous manipulation.

items.title: Post-Training, Finetuning, and Steering:A Field Guide for Curating Training Data
items.summary: While Vision-Language-Action models have enabled impressive cross-task transfer in zero-shot settings, \emph{adaptation} methods are often necessary to achieve consistent performance on novel tasks.

items.title: Collective Learning for Unified Robotic Manipulation via Predictive Dynamics Adaptation
items.summary: Learning a collective policy for state-based Cartesian manipulation across diverse robotic embodiments presents a fundamental challenge due to embodiment-dependent transition dynamics.

items.title: Learning in Orbit: Onboard Training and Closed-Loop Attitude Control with a Thermal Segmentation Model on a Spacecraft
items.summary: Deep space missions increasingly require spacecraft capable of autonomously operating in environments with communication delays and bandwidth limitations.

items.title: Benchmarking 3D Reconstruction for Under-Ice Robotic Perception in Arctic Environments
items.summary: As the Arctic transitions toward a seasonally ice-free state, capturing the complex morphology of submerged sea ice is crucial for advancing models of ocean-ice-atmosphere heat exchange and monitoring under-ice habitats.

items.title: DexMimic: A Generalist Dexterous Hand-Object Tracking Policy via Value-Guided Reset Allocation
items.summary: We introduce DexMimic, a generalist dexterous hand-object tracking policy jointly trained across diverse HOI trajectories. DexMimic realizes this insight through Value-Guided Reset Allocation, which adapts the initialization distribution online to prioritize difficult phases and select reset states with higher expected tracking returns.

items.title: Receding-Horizon Next-Best-View Planning for Highly Occluded Target Perception
items.summary: Robotic systems that must acquire information about a specific target often face severe occlusion from sur- rounding structures or from the target itself, such that a single camera viewpoint provides only partial information.

items.title: Tread: A Visuo-Inertial Framework for Terrain and Locomotion Context-Aware Gait-Phase and Speed Estimation in Wearable Robotics
items.summary: A wearable assistive robot must continuously estimate terrain, locomotion mode, gait phase, and walking speed. Anticipatory Terrain Perception (ATP) classifies incoming terrain with 96.3% accuracy and anticipates terrain transitions by 1.46 s on average.

items.title: RingNav: Task-Shaped Circular Memory for Visual Heading
items.summary: Tiny robots have limited computation and memory, yet visual navigation systems often maintain more state than a task requires. We present \textbf{RingNav}, a \(10.6\)k--parameter visual heading estimator that constrains its memory to the circular manifold \(S^1\).

items.title: Contact-UAN: Unsupervised Actuator Networks as a Residual World Model for Humanoid Control
items.summary: Humanoid policies trained in simulation can transfer qualitatively to hardware while failing to transfer the force interactions learned during training, compromising torque efficiency, load regulation, and robustness to impacts. We introduce Contact-UAN, a residual world model that preserves a simulator's physics priors while correcting actuator dynamics to align simulated rollouts with recorded hardware rollouts.

items.title: $\lambda_0$: Scaling Open-World Egocentric Human Data for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated whole-body interaction with the physical world, yet collecting robot demonstrations at scale remains costly. Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, but existing egocentric human supervision often omits locomotion and posture, while embodiment differences and controller dynamics hinder accurate end-effector execution.

items.title: Graph Coarsening Enables Escaping Local Optima in Compute-Constrained Nonconvex MAX-CUT
items.summary: Because its binary optimization landscape contains exponentially many local optima, MAX-CUT is highly sensitive to initialization. We warm-start PPR with Combinatorial Multigrid (CMG), a spectral graph-coarsening method that produces structure-aware initial solutions in near-linear time without training data.

items.title: Loss Curvature as a Sampling-Free Proxy for Memorization in Diffusion Models
items.summary: Understanding the mechanism behind why diffusion models memorize their training data remains an open question in generative modeling. In this paper, we examine this question from two perspectives: (a) the model-level perspective concerning the onset of memorization in a model during training, and (b) the sample-level perspective concerning the proclivity of an individual sample to be memorized by a given model.

items.title: Tracing Morphology, Semantics, and Divergence in Language Acquisition
items.summary: Understanding the dynamics of language acquisition in Large Language Models (LLMs) is crucial for uncovering how statistical representations evolve into structured linguistic capabilities. In this work, we leverage intermediate checkpoints from open-source models (e.g., Pythia and OLMo) under teacher-forcing evaluation to systematically investigate language acquisition across training steps and model scales.

items.title: Lag: A Mean-Field Optimal Policy for Online Assignment with Reusable Resources
items.summary: We study online task assignment with reusable resources. This problem arises in peer reviewer assignment, skill-based call routing, rideshare matching, emergency dispatch, and crowdsourcing: Tasks arrive according to a geometric process and must be immediately assigned to servers that become temporarily busy, yielding rewards that depend on the task-server pair.

items.title: Who Should We Listen to More? Welfare-Aware Preference Acquisition for Pluralistic Alignment
items.summary: Pluralistic alignment needs to accommodate diverse preferences under limited human feedback. We study how to allocate human feedback across people to construct training data for pluralistic alignment, and how this allocation affects the trained policy.

items.title: How Many Ranks Does a Token Need? A Noise-Floor Squelch for Rank-One LoRA Experts
items.summary: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) applies every rank-one component of its update to every token, and mixture-of-experts variants replace this with a learned router that activates a fixed number of components.

items.title: IR-PRM+ with Previous-Utility Prediction: Constant Regret and Best-Iterate Convergence
items.summary: Regret matching (and its variants) and counterfactual regret minimization are central algorithms in practice for normal-form and extensive-form game solving. Recent work introduced IREG-PRM+, a regret matching variant which does have strong theoretical convergence guarantees.

items.title: Scaling Cheap Synthetic Pretraining Improves Indoor Radio-Map Prediction
items.summary: Real measurements are too limited to train an accurate indoor pathloss predictor that works across a wide range of buildings. Despite simulator mismatch, our ResNet-101 model reduces error by 15% on average relative to the best known methods across five indoor radio-map prediction tasks and improves transfer on a small real-measurement dataset.

items.title: Data Density Scaling Laws for Image Self-Distillation
items.summary: Current scaling law formulations suggest that increasing the number of unique samples in a dataset improves model performance, while repeated exposure to the same samples provides diminishing value.

items.title: PMO-Dock: Benchmarking Docking, Specificity, and Generalization in Molecular Optimization
items.summary: The Practical Molecular Optimization (PMO) benchmark standardized evaluation in molecular optimization, but it is built on simple property-based oracles that do not capture structure-based drug design.

items.title: Token Utility for On-Policy Distillation via Local Trust-Region Optimization
items.summary: Token-selection methods for on-policy distillation (OPD) prioritize student-visited positions using diverse signals, including uncertainty, teacher-student disagreement, and mismatch direction.

items.title: Do Perturbation Predictors Learn Gene Interactions? Diagnosing Extrapolation in Agentic Screening
items.summary: High-throughput perturbation screens increasingly use machine-learning models to predict the effects of gene combinations that were never measured. We therefore compare each model prediction with a simple additive prediction obtained by summing the two observed single-gene effects.

items.title: Do Vision CIL Methods Transfer to Protein? A Diagnostic Benchmark of Frozen Protein Encoders
items.summary: Protein function annotation operates over an expanding label space, making class-incremental learning (CIL) a natural framework for incorporating newly discovered functions without full retraining. Yet existing CIL methods have been developed largely in vision and have not been systematically evaluated over frozen protein representations.

items.title: Inverse Reasoning Models for Efficient Post-Training and Verification from Answer-Only Data
items.summary: Post-training reasoning LLMs often requires making a tradeoff between costly supervision and compute inefficiency: supervised finetuning typically requires reasoning traces, which is data inefficient since in many applications one only has prompt-answer tuples and lacks the groundtruth chain-of-thought (CoT) sequence.

items.title: Lotus: Learning to Understand Time-series by Learning to Forecast
items.summary: Time-series language models typically align numerical signals with language using labels, captions, or question-answer pairs. We instantiate this principle in LOTUS, which divides each time-series channel into non-overlapping patches and maps them into the LLM embedding space.
